section_entries.label: 1. Introduction and statements
section_entries.mathematical_role: Defines the extended Selberg class, states zero-free and zero-count comparisons for positive and zero degree, and extends the question to imprimitive Dirichlet L-functions.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Derivative zeros still track zeros after deleting Euler factors
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: States the asymptotic equality of function and derivative zero counts, its degree-zero sharpening, and the imprimitive Dirichlet theorem where the removed Euler factors create a linear zero count on Re s=0.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Track zeros continuously through a symmetry-preserving deformation
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Defines an interpolation inside the extended Selberg class, justifies local zero trajectories by Rouche's theorem, explains collision and symmetric splitting, and derives ODEs for function and derivative zero paths.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Deleting finitely many Euler factors adds a bounded term to L'/L, so the remote sign and counting argument persist even though the Riemann-type functional equation is lost.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The source explicitly notes that more general nonfunctional-equation zeta functions need not show the same behavior.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Bounded multiplicative perturbations preserve the contour mechanism

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The source marks a genuine boundary for Speiser-style transfer: the proved mechanism extends to bounded modifications of extended-Selberg-class functions, but analogous computations for Hurwitz and Lerch zeta functions do not support the same equivalence.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The authors state that their theorem generalizes to extended-Selberg-class zeta functions multiplied by a simple function. They contrast this with Hurwitz and Lerch zeta functions, for which computations do not confirm the Speiser analogue.
directed.conceptual_reading: A familiar functional or zero symmetry is not alone sufficient; the proof depends on additional analytic structure present in the successful class.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The proposed bridge is classification by functional-equation and Selberg-class structure, with computation acting as a falsification check outside that class.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The negative observation is computational and source-specific, not an impossibility theorem for all formulations of a Speiser analogue.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence in the stated scope distinction; the excerpt does not provide the computational protocol or theorem definitions.

supported: The source says Theorem 1.6 extends to extended-Selberg-class zeta functions multiplied by a simple function and that computations do not confirm the Speiser equivalent for Hurwitz and Lerch zeta functions, which lack the Riemann-type functional equation.
inference: It is reasonable to infer that more analytic structure than superficial zero symmetry is needed.
unsupported_or_imported: The spontaneous phrase 'bounded modifications' is not in the source, and the exact additional sufficient structure is not identified by this short span.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: A generic analogy-boundary lesson could be pasted elsewhere unless it retains the precise positive class and negative computational cases.
context_or_ocr_risk: Theorem 1.6, 'simple function,' computation protocol, and candidate equivalence are outside the unit.
missed_mechanism: The excerpt does not show which step of the Levinson-Montgomery proof fails for Hurwitz/Lerch functions.
revision_instructions: Replace 'bounded modifications' with the source's 'multiplied by some simple function'; label the needed extra structure unresolved and the negative result computational only.

section_entries.label: 2. Computations
section_entries.mathematical_role: Builds a functional-equation-preserving interpolation, tracks function and derivative zeros, and uses the argument principle to revisit the Davenport-Heilbronn derivative-zero computation.

unit_result_entry.title: Argument-principle integrals correct a missed derivative-zero computation
unit_result_entry.why_material: Revisits the Davenport-Heilbronn example, finds derivative zeros corresponding in height to known off-line zeros, and explains how contour integrals count and locate derivative zeros before numerical root refinement.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: The contour count is exact in principle, but the reported Mathematica evaluation remains heuristic because accuracy was not explicitly controlled.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: Requires the displayed logarithmic-derivative contour integrals; extracted clearly.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Many critical-line zero pairs collide and leave under interpolation
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Reports how often computed zero trajectories leave the line and records a more complex three-zero/two-derivative-zero interaction that qualifies the simplest collision picture.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Functional symmetry makes F'/F point left on remote contours
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Applies Hadamard factorization to the completed function, pairs symmetric nontrivial zeros, and combines their contributions with gamma asymptotics to make Re(F'/F) negative in the far left half-plane.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Functional symmetry keeps a simple zero on the critical line; leaving requires collision into a multiple zero, where the derivative vanishes, after which paired trajectories can split symmetrically.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The detailed trajectories and frequencies are uncontrolled computations; only the local multiplicity implication is analytic.
related_synthesis_entries.title: A multiple zero is the hinge between function and derivative geometry

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Argument-principle integrals turn an unreliable root search into a count-and-localize workflow: first certify how many derivative zeros lie in a region, then recover a location moment, and only afterward refine numerically.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For the Davenport-Heilbronn function the authors report four derivative zeros to the left of the critical line near four known off-line zeros, correcting an earlier failed search. They count derivative zeros using the contour integral of the logarithmic derivative of the derivative and, when there is one zero, obtain its location from the corresponding first-moment contour integral before using FindRoot.
directed.conceptual_reading: Global contour invariants guard against missed numerical roots. Root refinement becomes the last step rather than the evidence for existence.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The argument principle bridges boundary evaluations to an interior zero count; a weighted contour integral bridges the count to a centroid/location; numerical root finding refines that certified target.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The contour identities are exact in principle, but the paper's Mathematica evaluations lack an explicit accuracy certification and depend on zero-free boundaries.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence in the certification logic; moderate confidence in the reported decimal roots absent controlled numerics.

supported: The authors correct a prior missed-root report, numerically find four derivative zeros, use logarithmic-derivative contour integrals to count zeros and, for a single zero, recover its location before FindRoot refinement.
inference: The count-then-localize-then-refine workflow is a strong conceptual reading.
unsupported_or_imported: Calling the contour evaluation a 'certification' overstates the evidence because the paper gives no interval/error control for its numerical quadrature or boundary nonvanishing.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: The global-invariant-versus-root-search contrast is useful but must not turn an exact formal identity into an unverified numerical certificate.
context_or_ocr_risk: OCR drops normalization factors in the contour integrals, and the reported Mathematica calculations are not rigorously certified.
missed_mechanism: The prerequisites that the boundary be zero-free and the integral be evaluated with controlled winding error are omitted.
revision_instructions: Use 'counting identity' or 'count-and-localize workflow,' not 'certify'; state the zero-free-boundary and numerical-error obligations explicitly.
